title: Multi-part parcel geometry: acreage-weighted impact measurement
purpose: Condition attached to the multipolygon-fail-closed fix per _decisions/2026-08-08_multipolygon_fail_closed_and_the_real_fix.md — test the hypothesis that multi-part parcels (MultiPolygon multi-part, Polygon-with-holes, or a MultiPolygon single-part that itself has holes) skew toward larger tracts, so the 0.67-0.74 percent by-COUNT figure understates the true value/acreage exposure.

source.accessMode: READ-ONLY SELECT only; no writes, no DDL, no data-run/apply
source.note: No PostGIS extension in this store (only plpgsql, vector). True polygon area (ST_Area) is unavailable. Area is computed as the WGS84 bounding-box rectangle in acres from the table precomputed west_lng/south_lat/east_lng/north_lat columns, converted via 1 degree latitude ~= 364000 ft and 1 degree longitude ~= 364000*cos(latitude) ft, 43560 sqft/acre. Bbox area is an upward-biased proxy for true polygon area (a polygon area is always <= its bbox rectangle area), and the bias is generally WORSE for irregular, elongated, L-shaped, or genuinely multi-part tracts than for compact single-ring rectangles — so the multi-part share of total acreage reported here should be read as an UPPER BOUND on the true acreage skew, not an exact figure. Directionally reliable for the yes/no question the decision record asks (does acreage share exceed count share materially), not for a precise dollar-per-acre exposure estimate.

classification.description: multi_part = TRUE for any of: Polygon with coordinates.length > 1 (interior rings / holes); MultiPolygon with coordinates.length > 1 (more than one part); MultiPolygon with exactly one part whose single part itself has interior rings (holed single part) — this last case matches the code fix fail-closed ruling (a single-part MultiPolygon is only safely reducible when that part has NO holes).

statewide.headline: 0.7436% of parcels by count are multi-part, but they account for 59.6949% of total bbox acreage statewide — an approximately 80.3x skew toward larger tracts, confirming the decision record hypothesis directionally and by a wide margin.

countyFipsNameNote: This table has no county-name column, only county_fips (five-digit state+county FIPS, e.g. 48021 = Bastrop). No county-name lookup table exists in this database; FIPS codes are reported as-is, consistent with the diagnostic report and the resolver own identity convention (county_fips:prop_id).
reversalCriteriaAssessment: Per the decision record: reverse the fail-closed interim ruling if the acreage-weighted measurement shows the affected parcels represent a materially larger share of value than 0.67 percent of count implies. This measurement shows 59.69% of statewide bbox acreage in multi-part parcels versus 0.74% by count — an approximately 80x skew, unambiguously material. Under the record own reversal criteria this measurement is grounds to move multi-ring support ahead of other queued work rather than waiting on the named trigger conditions (a) through (d). This is a measurement, not a decision — the actual reversal call is reserved for the operator per the decision record ownership; this executor was authorized to fix-closed plus measure, not to decide the reversal.
limitations: Area is bbox-rectangle acreage, not true polygon area (no PostGIS in this store) — see source.note above; treat the 59.69% figure as an upper bound on true acreage skew, not exact.
Per-county breakdown covers all 19 counties present in this store (not a sample of 20 — the store has exactly 19 distinct county_fips values), ordered by total parcel count descending.

multiPartCount here (41,166 statewide) differs from the earlier diagnostic report figure (approximately 37,185) because this measurement additionally counts the holed-single-part-MultiPolygon case as multi-part, per the code fix actual fail-closed ruling; the diagnostic report did not separately break that subclass out.
This is a read-only SELECT-only measurement. No database writes were made.
